‘Ali stood before the people and asked them to bear witness about what they had heard the Holy
Prophet saying about him at Ghadir al-Khum.

Thirty of the companions, including twelve Badris (those
who had fought in the Battle of Badr), stood up and said that they saw on the Ghadir al-Khum day the
Holy Prophet holding up Hazrat ‘Ali's hand and saying to the people:
"Do you know that I have greater claim on the believers than they have on their own selves?"

Then the Holy Prophet said: "Of whomsoever I am "maula" (master), this ‘Ali is his "maula"
(master)."

Sad plight of those who did not confirm hadith of Ghadir
Out of this gathering three men did not bear witness to the event.

One of them was Anas Ibn Malik, who
said that because he had become enfeebled with old age he had forgotten all about it.

He said: "If you are telling lies, may Allah afflict thee with leprosy, which even your turban would not
conceal."
No sooner did Anas stand up from his place when leprosy appeared on his body.
